{
  "hook": "El Reventón grows on decomposed granite sands at 1,000 meters in Cebreros' El Reventón vineyard, where 70-year-old Alicante Bouschet and Garnacha vines face fierce diurnal swings. That altitude etches bright acidity and quartz snap into the wine's dark plum skin and smoky core. Critics hit 97 points for the 2022, cementing its pull in Gredos' old-vine scene.",
  "wine_summary": "Comando G targets micro-sites in Sierra de Gredos, vinifying old-vine Garnacha and field blends with minimal intervention to spotlight terroir transparency. El Reventón stands out for blending Alicante Bouschet's pigmented pulp—delivering inky color and tannic grip—with Garnacha's brighter red fruit, all from biodynamic farming. This duo from Cebreros' granite slopes produces structured reds that rival Burgundy in tension, earning a devoted following among natural wine advocates.",
  "terroir_expression": "Decomposed granite and quartzite soils in high-altitude Cebreros release smoky minerality and firm tannins into El Reventón, while continental climate with nights dipping below 10°C locks in piercing acidity against the grapes' ripe dark fruit. The 1,000-meter elevation slows ripening, yielding concentrated blackberry and purple plum flavors laced with wet stone and graphite—textbook Gredos tension over power.",
  "vinification_summary": "Foot-trodden whole clusters ferment spontaneously with native yeasts, then age 14 months in neutral French oak to integrate structure without masking site. Co-fermentation (blending varieties from the start) amplifies synergy between Alicante Bouschet's color and Garnacha's perfume, preserving volatile freshness. Biodynamic practices ensure vine health on fragile granite, yielding vegan wines with electric purity.",
  "food_pairing": "Nashville hot chicken: cayenne heat meets the wine's grippy tannins and bright acidity to cut grease without clashing spice. Wood-roasted suckling pig: smoky granite notes echo the char, while dark fruit balances crispy fat. Lamb tagine with prunes: plush plum skin fruit absorbs the dish's braise, acidity refreshes the dried fruit sweetness. Cacio e pepe: sharp pecorino tang pairs with tannic backbone, pepper grounds the mineral edge.",
  "comparable_wines": "Bernabeleva Cepas Viejas Garnacha — fellow Gredos granite old-vines deliver similar tense minerality and red fruit precision. Forjas del Salnés Priest Vineyard Godello Tinto — high-altitude field blend matches the vibrant structure and smoky depth.",
  "style_profile": "Full-bodied dry red with grippy tannins and smoky granite drive",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Open 2022 after 2025 for integration; 2019-2020 drink through 2035. Store at 55°F in darkness to preserve tension.",
  "value_assessment": "$140-180 per bottle positions El Reventón against Clos Mogador Priorat ($90) or La Rioja Alta 904 ($65). The site's rarity and 97-point precision justify the premium—cheaper Garnachas lack this layered granite snap. Skip if you want easy fruit over tension.",
  "market_position": "Sommeliers slot this on natural wine lists at spots like Noma or Eleven Madison Park for its Gredos cult status. Collectors grab allocations via importers like Skurnik. Retail appears in high-end shops like Chambers Street Wines for dedicated followers.",
  "insider_take": "Alicante Bouschet's rustic edge bolsters Garnacha without drowning its finesse—most chase pure Garnacha and miss this blend's superior backbone. Buy if you crave Burgundy-like structure in Spain; skip for softer Riojas.",
  "aging_potential_years": 15,
  "drinking_window_min_years": 3,
  "drinking_window_max_years": 15,
  "sensory": {
    "acidity": 4,
    "tannin": 4,
    "body": 4,
    "sweetness": 1,
    "alcohol": 4,
    "color_intensity": "deep",
    "aroma_intensity": "pronounced",

    "complexity": "complex",
    "quality_level": "exceptional"
  }
}

parsed.hook: El Reventón grows on decomposed granite sands at 1,000 meters in Cebreros' El Reventón vineyard, where 70-year-old Alicante Bouschet and Garnacha vines face fierce diurnal swings. That altitude etches bright acidity and quartz snap into the wine's dark plum skin and smoky core. Critics hit 97 points for the 2022, cementing its pull in Gredos' old-vine scene.
parsed.wine_summary: Comando G targets micro-sites in Sierra de Gredos, vinifying old-vine Garnacha and field blends with minimal intervention to spotlight terroir transparency. El Reventón stands out for blending Alicante Bouschet's pigmented pulp—delivering inky color and tannic grip—with Garnacha's brighter red fruit, all from biodynamic farming. This duo from Cebreros' granite slopes produces structured reds that rival Burgundy in tension, earning a devoted following among natural wine advocates.
parsed.terroir_expression: Decomposed granite and quartzite soils in high-altitude Cebreros release smoky minerality and firm tannins into El Reventón, while continental climate with nights dipping below 10°C locks in piercing acidity against the grapes' ripe dark fruit. The 1,000-meter elevation slows ripening, yielding concentrated blackberry and purple plum flavors laced with wet stone and graphite—textbook Gredos tension over power.
parsed.vinification_summary: Foot-trodden whole clusters ferment spontaneously with native yeasts, then age 14 months in neutral French oak to integrate structure without masking site. Co-fermentation (blending varieties from the start) amplifies synergy between Alicante Bouschet's color and Garnacha's perfume, preserving volatile freshness. Biodynamic practices ensure vine health on fragile granite, yielding vegan wines with electric purity.
